canonical_statement: For a finitary classical propositional language and a fixed sound proof calculus for that language, every formula semantically entailed by a set of premises is derivable from those premises. The statement phase must select the concrete syntax, valuation semantics, consequence relation, and proof calculus before this becomes an exact formal target.
domain_and_universes: Provisional: a type of propositional atoms; finitary formulas generated by classical Boolean connectives; sets or finite contexts of formulas; Boolean valuations. Lean universe levels and context representation remain open.
quantifiers: if every Boolean valuation satisfying Gamma also satisfies phi
then phi is derivable from Gamma in the selected calculus
hypotheses: the object language is classical and finitary
semantic consequence ranges over all two-valued Boolean valuations
the syntactic consequence relation is generated by one explicitly selected sound calculus
conclusion: Gamma syntactically derives phi in the selected calculus.

alternate_encodings.target: every Boolean tautology is a theorem of an empty-context Hilbert calculus
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate specialization/equivalence after a checked deduction-theorem or finite-premise transport

alternate_encodings.target: every semantically valid propositional formula has a natural-deduction or sequent-calculus derivation
alternate_encodings.relationship: candidate only; requires checked equivalence between calculi

alternate_encodings.target: a truth-table decision procedure returns a derivation certificate for every tautology
alternate_encodings.relationship: constructive proof route, not statement identity

excluded_degenerate_cases: Intuitionistic, modal, infinitary, first-order, and many-valued completeness are excluded. Soundness, compactness, and decidability are separate results. An arbitrary or inconsistent proof relation may not replace the selected standard calculus.
foundation_profile: Open at intake: the intended finite truth-table proof is expected to need no choice, but classical meta-reasoning, quotients, extensionality, and actual declaration axioms require later audit.
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel plus the repository's pinned mathlib environment; exact imports, versions, and transitive declaration closure remain open.
computation_profile: No evaluator, tactic, reflection procedure, oracle, or generated certificate is credited at intake.
formal_system: Lean 4 + pinned mathlib candidate; the propositional calculus will be represented as object syntax rather than Lean's ambient Prop unless an exact checked encoding justifies otherwise.
source_revisions: See source_statement_crosswalk.md. Post (1921) is a primary historical source candidate for the tautology/theorem formulation; immutable source hash, precise theorem text, errata audit, and a modern premise-consequence source remain open.
freshness_and_revocation_policy: Invalidate on changes to the selected language, calculus, semantic or syntactic consequence relation, canonical claim, Lean target, imports/toolchain, source pins, foundation/TCB policy, or rev-5.6 standard.
status_boundary: This planned intake freezes a reviewable classical propositional scope and its exclusions. It does not yet choose or elaborate a Lean calculus, establish source fidelity, credit a proof candidate, or complete the theorem.
